metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, used for simulation calibration and evaluation.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper states data is available from the corresponding author upon request in the Data Availability section.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extracts (xi, yi) coordinates from raw video frames to create position matrices mt of size X by Y.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, generic extraction tool not named, matrix dimensions provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st
nodes_process.description: Stacks N consecutive position matrices after down-sampling to represent the traffic state st.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, stacking logic and parameters fully specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: Trains a CNN-based Q-network using experience replay, target networks, and multitask learning to predict Q-values, speed, and queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all hyperparameters and tools specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator
nodes_process.description: Evaluates the trained policy in a SUMO simulation of a real-world freeway segment over 20 experiments.
tools_mentioned: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU version not stated
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, simulation environment and parameters fully detailed.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Training convergence curves showing episode reward and mean travel time over 1 million frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training process and hyperparameters are well-defined, but raw traffic data is available only upon request.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9: Vehicle travel times in the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Mainline vehicle travel times (min) from 8:00 to 9:00 for No control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulation environment (SUMO) and scenarios are clearly described; data access is the primary bottleneck.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2: Mean travel times in 20 simulation experiments (s).
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of mean travel times (seconds) across 20 experiments for No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Detailed numerical results provided for 20 runs; relies on SUMO simulator and described parameters.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10: Temporal-spatial distribution of speed in (a) no-control; (b) PI-ALINEA; (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing speed distribution across distance and time for three control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visual representation of simulation outcomes; consistent with reported metrics but data is not public.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11: Queue length at the on-ramp.
nodes_sink.description: Time-series of queue lengths at the on-ramp for the three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear comparison of simulation outputs; methodology for queue measurement is standard in SUMO.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12: Relationship of queue length and red ratio for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plots showing the correlation between signal red ratio and resulting queue length.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Derived from simulation logs; relationship is clearly explained in text.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13: Queue length and occupancy for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Correlation analysis between mainline occupancy and on-ramp queue length.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Plausible derivation from simulation data; supports the claim of DRL using more than just occupancy.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of downstream traffic volume (veh/h) over time for the three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Standard simulation output; clearly supports the 'capacity drop' alleviation claim.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16: Travel time with perturbed input data.
nodes_sink.description: Sensitivity analysis showing travel time impact when specific subareas of video data are removed.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Perturbation method (removing subarea data) is well-described and results are clearly plotted clearly.
